claim: 京都学派是20世纪日本哲学家群体，依托东亚传统（尤其大乘佛教）与西方哲学方法对话；西田为公认开创者但无意立派；学派从未建立正式机构（至2003年西田哲学学会）
locator: SEP 'The Kyoto School' 开篇定义段与 §2.1
note: 开篇：'a group of 20th century Japanese philosophers who drew on the intellectual and spiritual traditions of East Asia, those of Mahāyāna Buddhism in particular, as well as on the methods and content of Western philosophy'；§2.1：'By all accounts Nishida Kitarō is the School's originator'；'never founded an academic institution or formed an official organization (at least until The Nishida Philosophy Association was founded in 2003)'。

claim: '京都学派'之名源于外部：土田杏村1926/27年著作称'所谓京都学派，创始人为西田'；1932年户坂润〈京都学派の哲学〉使名称定型并批评其为'日本的布尔乔亚哲学'
locator: SEP 'The Kyoto School' §2.1 'A History of External Naming'
note: 'Tsuchida Kyōson (1891–1934) wrote of "the so-called Kyōto School, the founder of which is Nishida" (Tsuchida 1927, 94)'；日文版1926年出而晚于英文写作；'Tosaka Jun's 1932 essay "The Philosophy of the Kyoto School" introduced the term "Kyōto-gakuha" still in use today, accusing the group of "bourgeois philosophy in Japan"'。

claim: Heisig 建议以西田、田边、西谷三人为核心'三角'界定学派；大橋良介给出三代名单；藤田正胜主张'网络'定义
locator: SEP 'The Kyoto School' §2.2—§2.3
note: Heisig：'follow the lead of Takeuchi Yoshinori (1913–2002) and define the School by triangulating it around the three leading figures of Nishida, Tanabe, and Nishitani'；大橋三代：第一代西田+田边，第二代久松、西谷、高坂(1900–1969)、下村(1900–1995)、高山(1905–1993)、鈴木成高(1907–1988)，第三代武内、辻村(1922–2010)、上田；藤田以'network'定义。

claim: 西方第一哲学问'存在是什么'，京都学派问'无是什么'；SEP 称之为 meontology（意味论）的第一哲学；'绝对无'以自我否定运作、是'普遍之普遍'
locator: SEP 'The Kyoto School' §3.1—§3.3
note: 'What is being?' vs 'What is nothingness?'；Eastern first philosophy as 'meontology'；绝对无 'functions through self-negation'、'the universal of universals'（后两语见 SEP 'Nishida Kitarō' 概念节）。

claim: 西田几多郎 1870—1945；纯粹经验→场所→绝对无→绝对矛盾的自己同一；行为直观、逆对应
locator: SEP 'Nishida Kitarō' 全文；青空文库作者页（生卒1870-06-17/1945-06-07）
note: SEP：pure experience 为 'one and only reality'；place 层级（being、relative nothingness、absolute nothingness）；acting intuition 例为艺术创作'formed mutually'；inverse correlation：神与有限自我 'inseparable but asymmetrically co-dependent'；'continuity of discontinuities'。
